Each municipality is assigned a single config which specifies the behavior of the web scraper. The web scraper traverses webpages by following links specified by filters within a config. A \`layer\_filter\` or \`next\_page\_filter\` specifies which links to follow using a Regex and/or Xpath expression.

## Fields

| Field Name | Type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| start\_urls | List of strings | List of URLs that web scraping starts at for a municipality. |
| allowed\_domains | List of strings | The web scraper will be restricted to these domains when executing for this municipality. |
| layers | integer | The number of layers (clicks a user needs in order to get from any page to a bylaw document). |
| get\_pdfs | boolean | If true, the links that the web scraper collects are links to PDFs.  |
| layer\_filter | filter | Selects the links to the next layer. Must end with ‘/@href’ if provided |
| next\_page\_filter | filter | Selects the links to the next page. Must end with ‘/@href’ if provided |
| name\_filter | filter | Selects the document name after the first layer. Must end with ‘/text()’ if provided |
| number\_filter | filter | Selects the document number after the first layer. Must end with ‘/text()’ if provided |
| year\_filter | filter | Selects the document year after the first layer. Must end with ‘/text()’ if provided |

## Layers

When traversing through a website, each ‘click’ that a user does to get to their destination counts as a layer. The scraper traverses the specified number of layers by following links that match the \`layer\_filter\`.

Ex. Lets say we wanted to access the ‘Accessible Parking By-law’ from [https://www.mississauga.ca/council/by-laws/](https://www.mississauga.ca/council/by-laws/):  
1st layer: [https://www.mississauga.ca/council/by-laws/](https://www.mississauga.ca/council/by-laws/)   
![][image1]  
2nd layer: [https://www.mississauga.ca/publication/accessible-parking-by-law/](https://www.mississauga.ca/publication/accessible-parking-by-law/)   
![][image2]  
3rd layer: [https://www.mississauga.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/06104036/Accessible-Parking-By-law-0010-2016.pdf](https://www.mississauga.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/06104036/Accessible-Parking-By-law-0010-2016.pdf) (done)  
![][image3]  
2 clicks were required, so this was 2 layers.

## Pages

In addition to layers, the user may need to traverse any number of pages in order to see each link. The links to traverse to different pages are selected using the \`next\_page\_filter\`. The number of pages to be traversed is indefinite, the web scraper will stop execution once it has visited all pages, provided that each page exists at a unique URL.

Ex. At [https://www.regina.ca/bylaws-permits-licences/bylaws/](https://www.regina.ca/bylaws-permits-licences/bylaws/) the \<a\> tag with the class “button-3” takes the user to the next page.  
![][image4]

## Filters

A filter is used for selecting links or attributes. It may consist of a regular expression, Xpath expression, or both. 

**Regular Expressions (Regex):** A pattern-matching syntax used to find bits of similar text in large textual inputs, it is supported by many platforms and programming languages. Some tutorials & resources:

* [Regex Tutorial \- How to write Regular Expressions \- GeeksforGeeks](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/dsa/write-regular-expressions/)  
* [Regular expression syntax cheat sheet \- JavaScript | MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Regular_expressions/Cheatsheet)  
* [RegExr](https://regexr.com/)

**Xpath:** A pattern-matching syntax used for searching through the data serialization format XML (eXtensible Markup Language). Since HTML is derived from XML, Xpath can be used to find HTML elements and get their text using \`text()\`. Some tutorials & resources:

* [XML Tutorial](https://www.w3schools.com/xml/)  
* [XPath Tutorial](https://www.w3schools.com/xml/xpath_intro.asp)  
* [Xpath cheatsheet](https://devhints.io/xpath)
